manifest_item.statement: For the displayed H_N(q²) action let C_N=Σ_w q^(2 length(w))=Π_(r=1)^N(1+q²+…+q^(2(r−1))). Then A_N²=C_N A_N and Ker A_N=Σ_i Ker(S_i+1). The two-factor kernel is the partial q-symmetric subspace, generated by its explicit loop-shifted U-orbits; its quotient relations are the FULL three-case straightening recurrence in the next Definition. At q=1 these are ordinary antisymmetry. No torsionfree-over-A argument or A0 quotient of Laurent A is used.
manifest_item.strategy: Factor A_N on both sides by(1+S_i) using paired Coxeter lengths. Hence S_i A_N=A_N S_i=Q A_N, so A_N²=C_N A_N. Let J=ΣKer(S_i+1); the paired-length factorization gives J⊂Ker A_N. For every x, (S_i−Q)x lies in Ker(S_i+1) because(S_i+1)(S_i−Q)=0. Thus modulo J, x S_w≡Q^length(w)x and x A_N≡C_N x. If A_N x=0 this gives C_N x∈J; C_N≠0 in the generic field proves x∈J. It also proves the splitting/idempotent quotient. For two factors compute S on the three residue cases and the complete l∈Z Bernstein recurrence: equal residues yield symmetric loop relations; unequal residues yield the base adjacent residue relation and its symmetric-loop shifts, whose gap induction is exactly the following three-case recurrence. This establishes the kernel on the ORIGINAL Laurent-loop vector space, not only a localization.

psi_fix(R_fix−1)=(a^-1−1)(S+1).
Multiplication by a^-1−1 is injective on the original Laurent-loop module, hence its kernel is EXACTLY Ker(S+1) there. Define R_op=P R_fix P, psi_op=1−q²a. This is KMPY's MAIN bar-Delta-plus (OPPOSITE our Delta) channel, with source b_j→our b_(j+1), source ground indexk→u_(1−k). Its q0 leading term is z^H_op b1⊗z^-H_op b2 and psi_op≡1 modq. The denominator psi_fix has constant1 atq0, so the geometric q-adic series is legitimate even though a weight space of the affinized tensor can be infinite. Multiplication by loop functions commutes with U-prime, the combination of S and identity intertwines U-prime, and ratios a have total d-degree0; hence R intertwines the full affine module. Keep coefficients LEFT: subtract identity and clear the denominator to get the displayed equality. No original Laurent vector is lost by clearing psi; a^-1−1 is nonzero in the Laurent domain acting freely, proving the stated kernel before localization. For Yang-Baxter, use the FINITE RESIDUE operators S0_i and external commuting scalar variables x,y: B_i(x)=(x−1)S0_i+(Q−1), Q=q². This is the R0(a) numerator after R_fix=R0(a)·s_loop; it is not a polynomial expansion of the full affine S_i against noncommuting loop a. manifest_item.title: The semi-infinite q-wedge Fock space and its q-adic topology
manifest_item.statement: For charge M form the algebraic direct limit of the finite wedge spaces by appending u_(M−N),u_(M−N−1),… to a prefix of length N. Equivalently quotient the eventually-vacuum tensor space by the local wedge kernels. Normal semi-infinite words have i_k=Lambda_k−k+1+M with Lambda a partition, and the vacuum is u_M∧u_(M−1)∧…. Let F_A=⊕_Lambda A|Lambda;M>, F0=⊕ A0|Lambda;M>, F_Z0=⊕ Z[q]|Lambda;M>. The full-field separated q-adic topology is induced by q^n F0, NEVER q^nF_A=F_A. A finite A0 label component completes to a Q[[q]] lattice, and its full-field component completes to Q((q)) tensor_Q(q)F_mu. Separately the finite Z[q] chart completes to a Z[[q]] lattice; that integral completion is not identified with Q((q)) or asserted to be a Q-vector topology. Fix j(M)∈{1,…,e}, M=j−ae. The vacuum P-weight Omega_M is normalized by Omega0=Lambda0 and Omega_M−Omega_(M−1)=wt(u_M). Explicitly if M=te+r,0≤r<e, Omega_M=Lambda_r−[e t(t−1)/2+t r]delta. A partition's weight is Omega_M−Σ_cells alpha_(content+M), and its size is a separate grading. The Cartan d eigenvalue is Omega_M(d) minus the number of residue0 cells, not partition size. No false Omega_M=Omega_(M−e)+delta periodicity is asserted.
manifest_item.strategy: Append the exact ground tail. If a finite word becomes nonnormal across the cutoff, integral straightening stays inside its index interval. A tail filled with every integer in that interval eventually forces any offending term to0; ordered words stabilize to the displayed beta-number partition words. Their independence follows from sufficiently large finite normal-basis independence. Thus the algebraic quotient/direct limit has this basis and Laurent/integral/local charts. In the A0 chart every nonzero finite coordinate has finite valuation, so the topology is separated; the A0 lattice completion is Q[[q]] and localization gives the full-field Laurent-series completion Q((q)); the separate Z[q] chart completion is Z[[q]]. The vacuum weights follow by adding one affine vector u_M; summing its loop power a(M)=(j−M)/e gives the explicit quadratic delta shift. This discharges charge rather than silently changing the full d-action. In charge0 Omega0=Lambda0 and residues remain c−r.

manifest_item.title: Level-one global-basis transition polynomials in the symmetric-group convention
manifest_item.axiom_use: Inherits the axiom of choice through [[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]] (and hence through [[thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero]]) for the decomposition of the Fock space into highest-weight components; the definition of the polynomials themselves and the pairing are choice-free. Consumers must carry the same assumption while it is used.
manifest_item.statement:
Work in the linear symmetric-group model of
[[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]: the
$\mathbb{Q}(q)$-linear isomorphism $J M_\mu = |\mu'\rangle$, the transported
action, bar and $A_0$ standard chart $(F_0)_{\mathrm{sym}}$, and the weight
$\operatorname{wt}(M_\mu) = \Lambda_0 - \sum_i m_i(\mu)\alpha_i$, with
$A = \mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]$.

**The basic module and its lower basis.** Let
$M_{\mathrm{sym}} := J^{-1}V(\Lambda_0) = J^{-1}M_{\mathrm{QG}}$ be the
transported highest-weight module of the vacuum; by
[[thm-restricted-partition-component-is-the-basic-crystal-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]
its crystal is the $e$-restricted component and its labels are the $e$-restricted
partitions. For an $e$-restricted $\lambda$ define
$$G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda) := J^{-1}G_{\mathrm{QG}}(\lambda'),$$
where $G_{\mathrm{QG}}(\mu)$ is the lower global (canonical) basis element of
the Fock space at the standard vector $|\mu\rangle$
([[thm-the-basic-representation-global-basis-is-unitriangular-in-the-partition-basis]]).
Then $G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda) \equiv M_\lambda \bmod q\,(F_0)_{\mathrm{sym}}$
and the family $\{G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda)\}$ is the transported lower global
basis of $M_{\mathrm{sym}}$, indexed by the restricted labels. Define the
**level-one transition polynomials in the symmetric-group convention** by the
finite weightwise expansion
$$G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda) = \sum_\mu d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)\, M_\mu ,$$
the sum being over the partitions $\mu$ of the weight of $\lambda$.

**Ambient polarization and ambient upper coordinates.** Define the ambient
polarization by $B(M_\mu,M_\nu) = \delta_{\mu\nu}$ on the standard basis, a
symmetric nondegenerate bilinear form on each finite weight space. Fix a weight
$w$ and let $V_w$ be the (finite-dimensional) weight space of
$F_{\mathrm{sym}}$; let $D_{\mathrm{rect}}$ be the matrix with columns the
coordinate vectors of $G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda)$ for the finitely many
$e$-restricted $\lambda$ of weight $w$, and rows the **standard** shapes
$M_\mu$, $\mu$ of weight $w$; let
$$H := D_{\mathrm{rect}}^{\mathsf{t}}\, D_{\mathrm{rect}} , \qquad G_{\mathrm{sym}}^*(\lambda) := \sum_\mu \bigl(D_{\mathrm{rect}}H^{-1}\bigr)_{(\mu,\lambda)}\, M_\mu^* ,$$
where $M_\mu^*$ denotes the ambient orthonormal dual frame of the standard
basis. The $G_{\mathrm{sym}}^*(\lambda)$ are the **ambient upper coordinates**
of the basic module: they are the unique elements of the basic subspace
$(M_{\mathrm{sym}})_w\subseteq V_w$ characterized weightwise by $B(G_{\mathrm{sym}}^*(\lambda), G_{\mathrm{sym}}(\lambda')) = \delta_{\lambda\lambda'}$,
and are viewed in the ambient standard frame; adding a vector of the
$B$-orthogonal complement in $V_w$ gives other ambient representatives with
the same pairings. The coefficients
$e_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q) := (D_{\mathrm{rect}}H^{-1})_{(\mu,\lambda)}$ lie in
$\mathbb{Q}(q)$ but need not be Laurent integral or polynomial. They are
coordinates in the ambient space and not a "standard basis of the basic
module"; the exact integral upper basis is the transported upper global basis of
[[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]], whose
restricted graded $A$-dual lattice is free weightwise and perfectly paired with
the basic lower $A$-span, while no lower-$A$ selfduality, no $A$-unit $H$ and no
full algebraic duality in infinite rank is implied. The restriction of $B$ to the basic module equals the normalized transported
contravariant form (proved in step 4.2), so these are the same upper vectors
viewed in the ambient standard frame and in their own integral dual lattice.
Upper bar is the adjoint bar
$\psi^\vee$ with its own dual infinity chart and weighted upper operators, not
the ordinary lower bar.

**The full ambient case.** On the whole Fock space the analogous matrix
$D_{\mathrm{full}}$, with columns the $G(\mu)$ over all partitions and rows the
standard shapes, is unitriangular (diagonal $1$, in $q\mathbb{Z}[q]$ below the
diagonal), and the dual matrix with respect to $B$ is
$$D_{\mathrm{full}}^{-\mathsf{t}},$$
which is Laurent integral because the inverse of a unitriangular matrix with
entries in $\mathbb{Z}[q]$ has entries in $\mathbb{Z}[q]$.

**A worked instance.** At $e = 2$ the restricted shape $\lambda = (1,1)$ has
$G_{\mathrm{sym}}(1,1) = M_{1,1} + q\,M_{2}$, so $D_{\mathrm{rect}}$ has the
single column $(q,1)^{\mathsf{t}}$, $H = 1 + q^2$, and
$$G_{\mathrm{sym}}^*(1,1) = \frac{M_{1,1}^* + q\,M_2^*}{1+q^2} = \frac{M_{1,1} + q\,M_2}{1+q^2},$$
an explicit ambient coordinate that is rational but not Laurent integral:
$1 + q^2$ is not a unit of $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]$. No specialization of the $d$
to decomposition numbers of Hecke algebras is asserted here without the
separate correct Hecke parameter hypotheses.
manifest_item.strategy: Transport the lower Fock basis by the linear transpose-label map J, preserving q; obtain the exact coefficient identity, symmetric dominance direction, same-core and full reflected-weight support. Work weightwise with the rectangular lower-column matrix D and ambient orthonormal form. D(0) has distinct coordinate columns, so H=D^tD satisfies H(0)=I and is field invertible; DH^-1 gives the unique upper vectors inside the basic subspace, with whole-ambient representatives differing by its orthogonal complement. Compute the e=2 rational coordinates and the full ambient transpose-inverse matrix separately. The finite node-count identity Nright+Nleft=N(lambda)-1 proves sigma-adjointness of the orthonormal form; normalized highest-weight form uniqueness identifies its basic restriction with the transported QG form. Thus these upper vectors form the restricted integral dual basis with perfect pairing, while rational standard coordinates imply neither lower-A selfduality nor an A-unit Gram matrix. Transport the exact adjoint upper bar, dual charts and weighted operators; preserve all linear/semilinear and Hecke-parameter boundaries.

manifest_item.title: The regular-partition label convention and the Mullineux crystal involution
manifest_item.statement:
A partition is **regular** if each positive part occurs with multiplicity $<e$,
and **restricted** if $\lambda_r-\lambda_{r+1}<e$ for every $r$. Conjugation
$C:\lambda\mapsto\lambda'$ is the comparison map between the regular and the
restricted models; it sends the residue $i$ to $-i$. It is **not** the
same-model sign involution.

On the regular basic crystal of
[[thm-the-empty-component-is-the-highest-weight-crystal-b-lambda-zero]] define
$M$ by negating all colors of a lowering path from the empty partition:
$M(f_ib)=f_{-i}M(b)$ for every edge, $M(\varnothing)=\varnothing$. The
restricted sign involution is the conjugate $CMC^{-1}$.

manifest_item.title: Standard Fock vectors expand in the upper global basis
manifest_item.statement:
Use the symmetric model $M_\mu=|\mu'\rangle$ of
[[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]], the
basic field subspace $V$ of the vacuum Fock space spanned by the restricted
lower vectors $G(\lambda)=\sum_\mu d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)M_\mu$ of
[[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]],
and the bilinear form $B(M_\mu,M_\nu)=\delta_{\mu,\nu}$. Define the **standard
coordinate functional** $\operatorname{Std}_\mu$ in the restricted integral
weight dual of the lower lattice by
$\operatorname{Std}_\mu(x)=B(x,M_\mu)$. The restriction of $B$ to $V$ is
nondegenerate; identify its field dual with $V$ via $B$ and denote by
$\pi(M_\mu)$ the vector representing $\operatorname{Std}_\mu$, equivalently the
$B$-orthogonal projection of $M_\mu$ onto $V$. This is the definition of $\pi$
used below, not an undeclared projection from a generic upper-basis definition.
If $G^*(\lambda)$ is the $B$-dual upper vector, then
$$\operatorname{Std}_\mu=\pi(M_\mu)=\sum_{\lambda\ \mathrm{restricted}} d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)\,G^*(\lambda).$$
At each content the restricted $\operatorname{Std}_\lambda$ form an $A$-basis of
the upper dual lattice, by the restricted dominance-unitriangular coefficient
minor. The full family of raw $M_\mu$ is the basis of the ambient standard
lattice; the full projected family $\operatorname{Std}_\mu$ is generally
redundant. The projection $\pi$ need not land in the lower integral lattice. In
$e=2$ one has $G_{11}=M_{11}+qM_2$ and
$G_{11}^*=(M_{11}+qM_2)/(1+q^2)$, exhibiting the possible field denominator.
The sums at fixed content are finite. Choice is inherited only from the
declared global-basis suppliers.
manifest_item.strategy: Use the true symmetric transition support: off-diagonal standard shapes dominate lower labels. The restricted minor is finite unitriangular and has a finite polynomial inverse; the particular ambient Gram matrix is invertible because H(0)=I. Restrict the standard-coordinate functional to the basic lower lattice, obtaining A-valued coordinates and its unique representing vector in the basic subspace. The local normalized form identification makes the inverse-Gram family the transported upper global basis, so finite dual-pairing computations give Std_mu=pi(M_mu)=sum_lambda d(lambda,mu)G^*(lambda). The restricted minor proves the restricted standard functionals are an upper integral-dual basis, while the full projected family can be redundant and lower integrality can fail. Contravariance makes the basic orthogonal complement stable, hence pi intertwines the action; transposing diagrams yields the canonical removal recursion. Choice is only inherited.

manifest_item.title: Graded decomposition numbers equal canonical-basis coefficients in characteristic zero
manifest_item.statement:
In branch (C0) of the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], for every partition
$\mu$ with content $\alpha$ and every $\lambda\in RP_\alpha$, the graded
composition multiplicity satisfies
$$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q=d_{\lambda,\mu}(q),$$
where $d_{\lambda,\mu}$ is the level-one global-basis transition polynomial of
[[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]];
equivalently
$[S(\mu)]=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$ in
$G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$, and $d_{\lambda,\mu}=0$ unless
$\lambda\unlhd\mu$. Specializing $q=1$ gives Ariki's ungraded
decomposition-number theorem
$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]=d_{\lambda,\mu}(1)$. Choice is inherited only through the
QG-8 global-basis suppliers.
manifest_item.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Branch (C0) of the regime, a partition $\mu$ with content $\alpha$,
the graded Specht module $S(\mu)$, and the transported identification
$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$.

[F1] The transported identification sends $[S(\mu)]$ to the standard Fock
vector $S_\mu=\pi(M_\mu)$
([[thm-graded-specht-classes-realize-standard-fock-vectors]]); and
$S_\mu=\sum_\lambda d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)G^*(\lambda)$ over the restricted
labels, with the same coefficients as the lower expansion, by
[[lem-standard-fock-vectors-expand-in-the-upper-global-basis]].

[F2] In branch (C0) the transported normalized self-dual simples $D(\lambda)$
map to the upper global basis vectors $G^*(\lambda)$ under
$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$
([[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]] (2)), and the
simple classes form a basis of the free $A$-module $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$
([[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (2)).

[F3] The transition polynomials have off-diagonal entries in $q\mathbb Z[q]$ and are supported
on $\lambda\unlhd\mu$ with diagonal $1$
([[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]);
the graded module group is the restricted direct sum of the blockwise groups
with forgetful maps $\zeta$ satisfying $\zeta(qm)=\zeta(m)$
([[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]).

[F4] The graded Specht module and its basis are those of
[[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]; the regime is
branch (C0) of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]].

[C1] Choice is inherited only through the QG-8 global-basis and Fock suppliers
([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Transport the Specht class.** Applying $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$ to $[S(\mu)]$ gives $S_\mu$ by [F1], and the expansion of the standard vector in the upper family is $S_\mu=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)G^*(\lambda)$ by [F1]; the coefficients are the transition polynomials of [F3]. [F1, F3]

2.1 **Replace the upper basis by the simple classes.** By [F2] the vectors $G^*(\lambda)$ are the images of the simple classes $[D(\lambda)]$ under the same isomorphism; applying $(\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke})^{-1}$ to step 1.1 therefore gives the expansion $[S(\mu)]=\sum_{\lambda}d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)[D(\lambda)]$ in $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ [F1, F2]. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 **Read off multiplicities and support.** Since the simple classes form a basis of the free $A$-module $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ by [F2], the coefficient of $[D(\lambda)]$ in the expansion of step 2.1 is the graded composition multiplicity $[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q$, and it equals $d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(q)$; the support statement $d_{(\lambda,\mu)}=0$ unless $\lambda\unlhd\mu$ is the triangularity of [F3]. [F2, F3, step 2.1]

4.1 **The ungraded specialization.** The forgetful map $\zeta$ specializes $q$ to $1$ and sends a graded composition series to an ungraded one with the same multiplicities [F3]; applying $\zeta$ to the expansion of step 2.1 gives $[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]=d_{(\lambda,\mu)}(1)$, Ariki's ungraded decomposition-number theorem. No new choice is made: [C1] is inherited. [C1, F3, F4, given] ∎

manifest_item.statement: Take $F=\mathbb C$, $\xi=-1$ (so $e=2$), level one $\Lambda_0$ and $d=2$. Both partitions of $2$ have content $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ in the charge-$0$ convention, so $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ is the only nonzero block and $H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}=\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$; its transported grading has $\deg t=2$ (the KLR block is the rank-two $e=2$ block $F[t]/(t^2)$ with $\deg y_2=2$). The graded Specht modules are the one-dimensional modules $S(2)=\mathbb C$ and $S(1,1)=\mathbb C$, both with trivial underlying action of $t$, and the graded composition series of $P$ is $0\subset tP\subset P$ with $tP\cong D\{2\}$, so $$[P]=(1+q^2)[D]\quad\text{in }G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}),\qquad [P]\notin\{[D],q^{\pm1}[D],\dots\}.$$ The restricted label is $(1,1)$ (since $(1,1)$ is $2$-restricted and $(2)$ is not), the edge degrees of the two shapes are $\deg(S(1,1))=0$ and $\deg(S(2))=1$, so the graded Specht classes are $[S(1,1)]=[D]$ and $[S(2)]=q[D]$, and the level-one Fock data give $G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}$ and $G^*(1,1)=(M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)})/(1+q^2)$; hence under the transported identifications of [[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]] $$[P]\longmapsto G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}=(1+q^2)G^*(1,1),\qquad [D]\longmapsto G^*(1,1).$$ The graded Cartan pairing of [[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]] has $h([P],[D])=1$ and $h([P],[P])=1+q^2$, while the graded composition multiplicity is $[P:D]_q=1+q^2$ (ungraded value $2$). manifest_item.statement: In the positive-characteristic nondegenerate level-one regime, the normalized cellular head dotD(lambda) for each restricted partition lambda is isomorphic, with shift zero, to the normalized simple of the same right crystal label lambda. Now let J(lambda) be the reduction of the characteristic-zero normalized simple of crystal label lambda, constructed using a rational Specht-generator lattice. Its graded word character equals that of the characteristic-zero simple. Choose an extremal word of this common character. In characteristic zero the reconstruction label is lambda; in positive characteristic the same word gives the same canonical B(Lambda) label. The displayed quotient is1 for the characteristic-zero simple, hence [J(lambda):D_crystal(lambda)]_q=1 in positive characteristic.

Independently, the corrected canonical Fock comparison and the upper expansion identify [J(lambda)] with the inverse image of the characteristic-zero upper vector. The restricted upper-transition minor is dominance-unitriangular. Invert it over Z[q,q^{-1}] and use the ACTUAL positive-characteristic cellular-head triangular expansion of restricted Specht classes. This gives [J(lambda)]=[D_cell(lambda)]+sum_{nu<lambda}a_nu(q)[D_cell(nu)]. These coefficients are the actual composition multiplicities because J(lambda) is a module; there is no asserted positivity from matrix inversion alone. Induct over a finite dominance refinement in the fixed root degree. Assume D_cell(nu)=D_crystal(nu) for the smaller labels. Since different crystal labels give different simple orbits, D_crystal(lambda) cannot be any smaller D_cell(nu). Its occurrence in J(lambda) therefore forces D_cell(lambda)=D_crystal(lambda). The characteristic-zero simple D(lambda) is normalized for finite vector duality, so each word component e(nu)D(lambda) has a symmetric graded dimension: its Laurent polynomial is unchanged by v -> v^{-1}. The descended generator-fixing anti-involution fixes every word idempotent; hence e(nu)D_psi J(lambda) is the graded vector dual of e(nu)J(lambda), and its graded dimension is the same symmetric polynomial. Therefore D_psi J(lambda) and J(lambda) have identical word characters. The completed local extremal-word character detection proves G0 character injectivity over the actual positive-characteristic field, so [D_psi J(lambda)]=[J(lambda)]. manifest_item.statement:
In branch (C0) of the regime of
[[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], with the normalized
self-dual simples $D(\lambda)$ and their normalized projective covers
$Y(\lambda)$ labelled by the crystal $B(\Lambda_0)=RP$ as in
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (4):

of the normalized self-dual indecomposable projective $Y(\lambda)$ to the lower
global basis vector $G(\lambda)$ for every $\lambda\in RP$;

2. the transported identification
$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}:G_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\to V_A(\Lambda_0)^\vee$
sends $[D(\lambda)]$ to the upper global basis vector $G^*(\lambda)$, form-dual
to $G(\lambda)$ under the highest-weight contravariant form;

module $V_A(\Lambda_0)$ and corresponds to projective indecomposables, while
the upper global basis is the dual-canonical basis and corresponds to simple
classes, and the labels are those of
[[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (4): the
crystal $B(\Lambda_0)=RP$, with a simple and its projective cover carrying the
same label. The passage from these crystal labels to the
cellular/Dipper--James parametrization of the simple modules is not asserted
here; it is established with the head classification later on this page;

4. specializing the grading $q=1$ via the forgetful maps $\zeta$ of
[[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]

manifest_item.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Branch (C0) of the nondegenerate level-one regime, the normalized
self-dual simples and projective covers, and the transported identifications.

[F1] The QG-8 transport identifies the KLR-side canonical data with the
Hecke-side groups: clause (1) transports $\phi$ to $\phi^{\rm Hecke}$, clause
(2) transports $\Psi_{\rm can}$ to $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$, and clause (4)
identifies the transported normalized self-dual projectives with the lower
global basis, the transported normalized self-dual simples with the upper
global basis, and the transported crystals with the $B(\Lambda_0)$-crystals
labelled in $RP$ ([[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]]).

[F2] The lower and upper global bases, their duality
$B(G(\lambda),G^*(\lambda'))=\delta_{\lambda\lambda'}$ under the contravariant
form, and their crystal compatibility are those of
[[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]],
[[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]] and
[[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]]; the KLR
side conclusions are
`thm-self-dual-indecomposable-cyclotomic-klr-projectives-give-the-lower-global-basis`
and `thm-self-dual-simple-cyclotomic-klr-modules-give-the-upper-global-basis`.

[F3] The transport of the graded module category, its Grothendieck groups, its
Cartan and forgetful maps and its dualities along the blockwise graded
isomorphism is the content of
[[lem-graded-algebra-isomorphism-transports-the-graded-module-category]]; the
forgetful maps satisfy $\zeta(qm)=\zeta(m)$
([[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]).

[F4] The Specht classes realize the standard Fock vectors
([[thm-graded-specht-classes-realize-standard-fock-vectors]]), with the
restricted coordinate functionals and the transition polynomials of
[[lem-standard-fock-vectors-expand-in-the-upper-global-basis]] and
[[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]].

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Projectives to the lower basis (1).** By [F1] the transported isomorphism $\phi^{\rm Hecke}$ is the QG-8 transport of the KLR-side identification, under which the normalized self-dual indecomposable projectives correspond bijectively to the lower global basis; the transport preserves the classes of the underlying modules and internal shifts, so the class of $Y(\lambda)$ is sent to $G(\lambda)$ for every restricted label $\lambda$ [F1, F2]. 1.2 **Simples to the upper basis (2).** The same clause identifies the transported normalized self-dual simples with the upper global basis, and the upper family is form-dual to the lower family under the contravariant form by [F2]; hence $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}([D(\lambda)])=G^*(\lambda)$ with $B(G(\lambda),G^*(\lambda'))=\delta_{\lambda\lambda'}$ [F1, F2]. 1.4 **The ungraded specialization (4).** The forgetful maps satisfy $\zeta(qm)=\zeta(m)$ and specialize $q$ to $1$ [F3]; a graded composition series of a finite-dimensional graded module specializes to an ungraded composition series with the same multiplicities, and the transported identifications therefore specialize to the ungraded statement that the self-dual projective classes are the canonical basis and the simple classes the dual-canonical basis of the basic module, which is Ariki's ungraded canonical-basis statement [F1, F3]. Combining this specialization with the graded decomposition theorem of this page gives the ungraded decomposition-number statement; that combination is recorded as the pointer in clause (4) and is not used in the present proofs [F3, F4].
